title: introduce-fallback-prober-and-token-stitcher-to-harden-constraint-backends
author: Marcos Rivera
description:
Context: Users continue to see rare streaming corruption and malformed function-call framing when using combined constraint backends (CFG + regex) with aggressive tokenizers (BPE/bytepair variants). Root causes we identified: 1) constraints chosen by the muxer sometimes fail mid-subtoken boundary when a cached prefix crosses constraint transitions, 2) sampling fallbacks to lower-priority backends are opaque to the streaming layer and can produce partial token emissions, and 3) the OpenAI-compat tool/function-call framing assumes whole-token boundaries that our tokenizer sometimes splits across bytes.

What this PR does: Adds two coordinated subsystems and supporting fixes: 
- Fallback Prober: a light-weight runtime probe that validates candidate fallback backends before permitting an immediate streaming switch. The probe runs a short deterministic prefix evaluation (<=8 tokens) through the target backend with the current KV cache snapshot to ensure it will not emit token fragments that violate the active framing policy. If the probe fails, the muxer uses the next candidate or raises a controlled degrade-to-synchronous mode.
- Token Stitcher: a tokenizer-aware streaming post-processor that detects subtoken splits at constraint boundaries and stitches byte/subtoken fragments into emission-safe units. This avoids partial tool-call markers and broken JSON fragments when model tokenizers slice across punctuation or escape sequences.
- OpenAI-compat streaming adapter updates: preserve function-call sentinel token grouping by deferring emission until the stitcher confirms boundary integrity; extended compatibility tests for toolcall framing in both UTF-8 multi-byte and mixed-encoding prompts.
- Constraint backend changes: small CFG sampler change to expose deterministic-probe mode, regex backend guard to reject matches that would split an ongoing subtoken prefix.
- Observability: new metrics (constraint.probe.success, constraint.probe.latency_ms, stitcher.rate, stitcher.stitched_tokens) and a Console dashboard tab to inspect probe rejections and stitch operations in-flight.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc in PR thread and docs/constraints/architecture.md updated
- [x] Unit tests for probe and stitcher modules
- [x] Integration e2e test with streaming + toolcall in CI (flaky cases reproduced locally)
- [x] Benchmarked perf impact: median token latency +0.8ms, p95 +3.2ms under high batching load; cost-neutral when probe bypasses via short-circuit hits
- [x] Added metrics and console wiring
- [x] Backwards-compatible by default; feature gated behind runtime flags (constraint.probe.enabled=true, stitcher.enabled=true)

Testing: 
Single-node unit tests for edge tokenizers (tests/unit/token_stitcher_test.py) cover multi-byte UTF-8, zero-width joiners, and bytepair split cases. Integration tests (tests/integration/constraint_backends_test.py) exercise fallback paths between CFG -> regex -> null-backend with streaming on/off. Ran the system against our internal benchmark lab and reproduced the original corruption case on a small prompt set (attached example in discussion). CI includes a new e2e streaming job (ci/e2e/streaming-constraint) that was green on the final run.

Rollout plan: feature gated with flags. Start with dedicated/alpha customers with sampling telemetry enabled, monitor constraint.probe.success and stitcher.rate, then flip on for broader clusters after 2 weeks of stable metrics. Emergency rollback: set runtime flag constraint.probe.enabled=false OR stitcher.enabled=false to revert behavior without redeploying runtime.

Related: ENG-1123 (design), ENG-2100 (observability), SUP-4217 (customer-reported corruption incident).

Notes: This is intentionally conservative: the probe avoids invoking heavyweight decoding and uses a deterministic low-branch sampling mode to keep latency bounded. The stitcher is written defensively to avoid altering legitimate token sequences; it only coalesces fragments when it detects a violation of framing invariants (e.g., unclosed JSON braces inside a function-call envelope).

Change summary (high level): updated constraint muxer and backends, added runtime probe and stitcher modules, wired console metrics and dashboard, added unit/integration/e2e tests, small docs update.

review_thread: Ava: Can the probe ever slow tail latency for p50? How do we ensure it doesn't add extra decoding in the fast path?

Author (Marcos): Probe runs deterministically up to 8 tokens and short-circuits on a successful confidence check. We added a muxer optimization to bypass probing when the candidate backend has an identical tokenizer and KV-shape; added perf numbers in PR description and bench results in benchmarks/streaming/constraint_probe_latency.sql.
Lars: Token stitcher looks good; please add more comments around the heuristic thresholds and a safety clamp to avoid infinite buffer growth.
Author: Added safety clamp and comments; included unit test that simulates long-fragment streams to assert bounded memory usage.
Priya: Are there any corner cases where composing stitcher+probe could mask genuine model regressions? We want to be sure we're not hiding quality drops.
Author: Good point — stitcher only modifies emission when framing invariants are violated; we also added quality-metric alerts (console) for stitcher activity spikes so we can surface regressions.
Ava: Approved after verifying CI e2e job passed and perf impact is acceptable.
Merging: Ethan Zhao performed squash-merge after approvals and green CI.
merge_outcome: squash-merge by Ethan Zhao; commit message normalized to include ENG-1123 and release notes
release_notes:
- Added runtime fallback prober to validate backend switches for constrained decoding (opt-in via flags).
- Added tokenizer-aware Token Stitcher to prevent partial-token emissions across constraint boundaries, reducing streaming corruption for tool/function calls.
- New metrics and console dashboard for probe/stitcher activity.
- Backwards compatible and disabled by default; enable via runtime flags for gradual rollout.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated. To disable quickly: set constraint.probe.enabled=false and stitcher.enabled=false in runtime flags; monitor constraint.probe.success and stitcher.rate metrics after toggling. If customers report toolcall corruptions after enabling, roll back flags immediately and capture traces using scripts/trace_examples/reproduce_corruption.sh
security_considerations: No secret/material change. Probe runs deterministic short decodes on existing KV snapshots; does not introduce new network calls. Token stitcher observes emitted bytes but does not alter request payloads; instrumentation added to metrics is aggregated and does not include PII.
